 nipped worm] OED 3a defines nipped as ‘pinched, compressed, tightly squeezed’ and uses Autumn
as an example of this definition. Lloyd N. Jeffrey in ‘Shelley’s “Plumèd Insects Swift and Free” ’, K-SJ xxv

feeble under the trees and shrubs’. Worms are cold-blooded, and therefore their behaviour is highly
affected by changes in temperature: S.’s worm is nipped because in winter its movement is reduced.

15 The blithe swallows are flown, and the lizards each gone
To his dwelling;
Come months, come away,
Put on white, black, and grey,
Let your light sisters play —
20 Ye, follow the bier
Of the dead cold year,
And make her grave green with tear on tear.
